source: docs/research/hooks-deep-dive.md (checked 2026-09-29): §1.4 ARCHETYPES, §2.5 pairings, §2.6 VISUAL_HOOKS, §3.6 VARIANT_POLICY, §4.1 HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES, §5 RISKY_PHRASES, §6 proposed rules. Blocks are verbatim; 'maker' is WS-HOOKS glue (our inference, grade A).

curiosity-gap.definition: Names a specific unknown about the product that the payoff reveals on screen.
curiosity-gap.mechanism: Information-gap curiosity (Loewenstein 1994): a salient, closable gap motivates watching; forward reference speeds involuntary attention (ERP 2022).
curiosity-gap.evidence: Motion Curiosity 11th of 25 by hit rate [M]; OpusClip Direct Address/Intrigue/Question 1,768 mean views vs 1,879 TikTok median [M]; forward-reference headlines no worse than plain ones (CME 2016) [M]; vague withholding demoted by Meta, unpaid promises removed by YouTube [P].
curiosity-gap.when: demo, review, showcase: a concrete non-obvious detail is shown before 85% of runtime
curiosity-gap.avoid_when: payoff cannot name the hidden thing (D35); secret/industry framing; gap refers to 'this/it' with no noun
curiosity-gap.risk: medium: clickbait demotion if vague or unpaid
requires: a concrete detail the payoff shows (D35)
templates: Before you buy a {category}, check this.

bold-claim.definition: A specific, checkable performance claim the video proves in one take.
bold-claim.mechanism: Expectancy violation plus commitment: a falsifiable claim invites the viewer to verify it.
bold-claim.evidence: Motion Bold Claim 14th, Shocking Statement 16th; interrupt cluster, higher variance [M]; FTC requires a reasonable basis for objective claims; TikTok bans exaggerated results and absolutes (Apr 2026) [P].
bold-claim.when: demo formats with a measurable (time, count, before/after) captured on camera
bold-claim.avoid_when: superlatives (best, #1, only); health or efficacy; 'obsolete'; comparisons not filmed (D141)
bold-claim.risk: high: absolute or unsubstantiated claim class (D141)
requires: on-screen measurement or one-take demo proving the claim (D5)

negative-command.definition: Tells the viewer to stop one specific mistake; the payoff shows the fix.
negative-command.mechanism: Negativity bias and loss framing; the imperative interrupts passive scrolling.
negative-command.evidence: Each negative word +2.3% CTR (Robertson 2023); negative-emotion words beta 0.18 (Gligoric 2023) [S]; Motion Reverse Psychology 15th, Warning 18th [M]; OpusClip calls imperatives the most divisive pattern [A].
negative-command.when: advice, tools, kitchen, beauty: a real common mistake with a visible fix
negative-command.avoid_when: no concrete mistake; shaming; health scares; 'stop scrolling' attention bait
negative-command.risk: medium: sensational if the mistake is invented
requires: a real {mistake} and its fix on screen
templates: Don't buy a {category} before checking this.

proof-first.definition: Opens on sourced evidence (rating, measurement, result card) before any claim.
proof-first.mechanism: Credibility heuristic: evidence first lowers skepticism for the rest of the video.
proof-first.evidence: Motion Testimonial format 6.5% winner rate, Statistic format listed [M]; OpusClip specific-number pattern [A]; FTC 16 CFR 465 and D136 ban unsourced ratings and counts [P].
proof-first.when: the prompt supplies proof with its source
proof-first.avoid_when: proof not in the prompt (D136); AI presenter framing proof as personal experience (D137)
proof-first.risk: high if unsourced: fabricated review signal
requires: proof in the prompt, attributed (D136)

transformation.definition: Before and after of the same object, with the product as the cause.
transformation.mechanism: Visual contrast and closure: the gap between the two states is the promise.
transformation.evidence: Motion Before & After 6th of 25 formats [M]; OpusClip showcase class includes before/after (6,037) [M]; TikTok bans misleading before/after and unsupported transformation claims [P].
transformation.when: honest matched-framing results on objects: cleaning, cooking, organizing, car care
transformation.avoid_when: body, skin, weight or health results; staged timelines; AI-generated results
transformation.risk: medium-high: misleading before/after is an ad-rejection class
requires: real matched before/after footage
dates if multi-day
templates: This is the after. Here's the before.

story-time.definition: Opens mid-story with the conflict already stated.
story-time.mechanism: Narrative transportation: an unresolved conflict pulls toward the resolution.
story-time.evidence: OpusClip: story-setup openers underperform [A/M]; Motion Storytelling only on the spend-use list [M]; first-person singular helps headlines (beta 0.24) [S].
story-time.when: human presenter; vlog, challenge, routine; conflict in the first line
story-time.avoid_when: AI presenter (D137); slow setup; the story is not true
requires: presenter=human
a true lived experience
templates: I didn't expect the {product} to win.

contrarian-reframe.definition: Rejects a common practice and promises a better one, shown on screen.
contrarian-reframe.mechanism: Schema violation: viewers stay to resolve the contradiction.
contrarian-reframe.evidence: Motion Contrarian 20th, Myth Busting on the spend list; interrupt cluster, high variance [M]; OpusClip lists the contrarian open and warns against crying wolf [A]; current templates fit D73 0/2.
contrarian-reframe.when: advice or education with a widespread practice and a demonstrable alternative
contrarian-reframe.avoid_when: strawman beliefs; health myths; value claims without a comparison
contrarian-reframe.risk: medium: misleading if the alternative is not shown
requires: a real {common} practice
the alternative shown

identity-reveal.definition: Leads with who is speaking: a real credential or role, or the AI disclosure itself.
identity-reveal.mechanism: Source credibility and in-group identity; disclosure pre-empts distrust.
identity-reveal.evidence: Motion Authority 25th, Founder 20th and Expert Explained 25th formats [M]; OpusClip expert-explainer is the most common storyline (2,626 clips) [M]; 'I' helps headlines (beta 0.24) [S]; FTC bans fake testimonialists (16 CFR 465.2) [P].
identity-reveal.when: human with a verified relevant identity; AI only as a disclosure-first opener
identity-reveal.avoid_when: unverifiable credentials; AI claiming a human identity (D137; Llama AUP)
identity-reveal.risk: high if the identity is fabricated
requires: identity from the prompt (human) or {persona_note} (AI)

problem-agitate.definition: Names the viewer's problem vividly before the product appears.
problem-agitate.mechanism: Problem salience plus negativity; self-relevance holds the viewer for the fix.
problem-agitate.evidence: Motion Problem Agitation format 15th [M]; negativity lifts CTR (Robertson; Gligoric) [S]; problem-to-solution is the standard explainer template (Jasper) [A].
problem-agitate.when: utilitarian products with a visible, common frustration
problem-agitate.avoid_when: medical conditions, body image, fear appeals; problem not shown
requires: the {flaw} visible in frame 0 (problem-state)

question.definition: Asks the specific question a viewer would search; the payoff answers it explicitly.
question.mechanism: Self-reference and search intent; an answerable question sets up an expected answer.
question.evidence: Mixed [M]: self-referencing questions beat declaratives (Lai & Farbrot 2014); questions lowered CTR or attitudes (Kuiken 2017; CME 2016; Jung 2022); OpusClip question class below median; Motion If/Then 17th, Direct Address 23rd.
question.when: 'worth it', 'X vs Y', 'does it work' intents; verdict payoffs; keyword first (DISC-01)
question.avoid_when: rhetorical or vague questions; questions answerable 'no' instantly; health questions
requires: a payoff that answers the question in words and on screen

comparison.definition: The product against its alternative on one filmed test.
comparison.mechanism: Contrast supports the decision; the winner is the payoff.
comparison.evidence: Motion Split Screen 8th, Us vs Them 9th formats; Contrast tactic 22nd [M]; TikTok allows comparative claims only with evidence [P].
comparison.when: a pricier, DIY or older alternative exists and both can be filmed
comparison.avoid_when: named competitor brands with claims; rigged setups
requires: real footage of both on the same test

pov.definition: Puts the viewer inside a concrete scenario with 'POV:'.
pov.mechanism: Self-projection and relatability: second person without asking a question.
pov.evidence: Motion POV format 18th, Relatability tactic 21st [M]; internal pack lists pov among top families [A]; RULES saturation note on repeated 'POV: your {domain}...' [A].
pov.when: routines, lifestyle, relatable moments; pairs with pov-hands
pov.avoid_when: POV as a bare label; the same POV frame across a series
requires: the scenario is what the footage shows

newness.definition: Frames the product, version or use as new, or as a first look.
newness.mechanism: Novelty seeking: 'new' signals information the viewer lacks.
newness.evidence: Motion Newness 1st and New Product Announcement 8th by hit rate, inflated by the promo window [M].
newness.when: the prompt states a launch, new version or new use; otherwise only 'first look' templates
newness.avoid_when: product is not new; launch urgency that is not real
requires: a newness fact in the prompt for templates containing 'new'
templates: First look at the {product} in action.

confession.definition: Admits a real mistake or bias before showing what changed.
confession.mechanism: Vulnerability and the pratfall effect: admitted fault raises credibility.
confession.evidence: Motion Confession 9th by hit rate and over-indexes on spend; interrupt cluster, high variance [M]; 'I' helps headlines (beta 0.24) [S].
confession.when: human presenter; beauty, wellness, lifestyle, money; confession tied to the payoff
confession.avoid_when: AI presenter (D137); invented confessions (FTC 465); health overshare
requires: presenter=human
a true confession
templates: I almost didn't post this {product} test.

price-anchor.definition: States the supplied price against a pricier alternative or an outcome.
price-anchor.evidence: Motion Price Anchor 3rd by hit rate, 2nd by spend use [M]; FTC lists fake discounts as a dark pattern; TikTok bans inconsistent price details [P]; D37.
price-anchor.when: the prompt gives a price; dupes and value reviews
price-anchor.avoid_when: no price in the prompt (D37); was/now without a real prior price; 'cheapest'
price-anchor.risk: high if the price is invented or the discount fake
requires: price in the prompt (D37)

listicle.definition: Promises a counted set and delivers exactly that count.
listicle.mechanism: Structure and progress: a count sets a closable expectation.
listicle.evidence: Motion Listicle format 7th, Reasons Why on the spend list [M]; OpusClip specific-number pattern [A].
listicle.avoid_when: beats do not deliver the stated count; padding
requires: beats deliver exactly the stated count
'tested' templates need that many real products

challenge.definition: A time-boxed personal test stated as the hook: streak, quit, only-X.
challenge.mechanism: Stakes and completion curiosity: will it last?
challenge.evidence: OpusClip Rare Event/Achievement 2,983 mean views, 2nd named class [M]; D52 pins challenge hooks to the day count; TikTok keeps extreme dieting and fitness out of the FYF [P].
challenge.when: human creator; habits, food, fitness, digital detox; dated footage
challenge.avoid_when: dangerous or extreme diet challenges; AI presenter doing the challenge
challenge.risk: medium: FYF ineligibility or dangerous-acts policy
requires: presenter=human, or a licensed creator log narrated in curator framing (D39)

day-counter.definition: Opens on a day-N marker from an ongoing, dated log.
day-counter.mechanism: Progress cue plus accumulated proof: the number implies commitment.
day-counter.evidence: D52 pinned day-counter hooks [A]; OpusClip Rare Event/Achievement 2,983 [M]; specific numbers imply measurement [A].
day-counter.when: routines, challenges, long-term product tests with dated footage
day-counter.avoid_when: no real log; hook day differs from payoff day (D5 drift)
requires: a dated log; hook day equals payoff day (D52)

showcase.definition: Shows the product working, or the finished outcome, before any explanation.
showcase.mechanism: Immediate value preview: no setup stands between the viewer and the payoff image.
showcase.evidence: OpusClip Product/Outcome Showcase top class, 6,037 mean views [M]; product on screen early +65% brand affinity (Creative Codes, SFV) [S]; Motion Demo 8.1%, Unboxing 9.8% [M]; TikTok Shop wants the hook about the product [P].
showcase.when: any visually demonstrable product; roundups; room, car or desk showcases (D81)
showcase.avoid_when: static product shots (TikTok Shop non-interactive cap); nothing moves in frame 0
requires: real footage of the product working

product-in-action.evidence: Motion Demo format 8.1% winner rate, 2nd [M]; OpusClip showcase class top at 6,037 mean views [M]; product on screen early +65% affinity, +25% recall (Creative Codes) [S]; TikTok Shop wants >=3 s dynamic footage and a product-led hook [P].
product-in-action.needs: the product mid-task with hands in frame and visible motion by 0.5 s; the real product sound
product-in-action.ai_render_risk: medium: hand and finger artifacts, liquid physics, invented logos (D64 negative prompt)

result-reveal.evidence: OpusClip: leading with the outcome is the top pattern [M]; Motion Before & After 6th [M]; TikTok bans results that give a false impression [P].
result-reveal.needs: a real captured result that the payoff re-shows in context
result-reveal.ai_render_risk: high: a generated result is a fabricated claim; use real capture only

before-after-split.evidence: Motion Before & After 6th, Split Screen 8th [M]; TikTok ad policy restricts before/after without evidence; TikTok Shop bans unsupported transformations [P].
before-after-split.needs: matched framing, light and angle; dated captures; label pair 'BEFORE | AFTER' (D144)
before-after-split.ai_render_risk: high: never generate either side; composite real footage

problem-state.evidence: Motion Problem Agitation 15th [M]; negativity lifts clicks (Robertson 2023; Gligoric 2023) [S, text-to-visual inference].
problem-state.needs: the problem at its worst, honestly depicted; the product enters by about 3 s
problem-state.ai_render_risk: low-medium: staged mess reads fine; avoid depicting injury or health symptoms

pov-hands.evidence: Motion POV format 18th [M]; hands-on-product openers are practitioner consensus [A].
pov-hands.needs: first-person angle, the viewer's hands using the product, motion by 0.5 s
pov-hands.ai_render_risk: medium-high: hands are the most common generation artifact

face-reaction.evidence: Visible human +27% CTR (Meta, SFV) [S]; faces predict TikTok views better than text sentiment (163k videos, SFV section 7) [M]; Motion Testimonial 6.5% [M].
face-reaction.needs: presenter face with the product or result in the same frame; human presenter for emotional reactions
face-reaction.ai_render_risk: high: an AI face reacting to a result implies use (D137); keep AI expressions neutral and disclosed (D138)

text-first.evidence: Motion Headline format 4th [M]; TikTok search ads recommend a keyword text hook [P]; text stickers +11 points (Meta, SFV) [S]; brief key-phrase labels aid retention (Mayer & Johnson 2008) [S].
text-first.needs: a <=3-word card over MOTION (never a static card, per TikTok Shop's non-interactive rule), keyword head noun included
text-first.ai_render_risk: low: composite the text in post, never ask the model to draw it

unboxing.evidence: Motion Unboxing 9.8% winner rate, highest in its table, but only 2.1% of creatives [M].
unboxing.needs: a real package opened mid-action; packaging branding must be real, not invented (D37/D64)
unboxing.ai_render_risk: medium: garbled packaging text and invented brands

comparison.evidence: Motion Us vs Them 9th, Split Screen 8th, Contrast tactic 22nd [M]; TikTok allows comparative claims only with evidence [P].
comparison.needs: both items filmed on the same test, same framing; no named-competitor claims
comparison.ai_render_risk: medium: both sides must be real captures when the outcome is the claim

day-counter.evidence: D52 pinned day-counter hooks [A]; OpusClip Rare Event/Achievement class 2,983 [M].
day-counter.needs: a 'DAY N' label over real footage from that day; the hook's N equals the payoff's N
day-counter.ai_render_risk: low for the label; lived-experience risk if an AI presenter claims the streak (D137)

satisfying-macro.evidence: ASMR audio raised ad recall across 4 experiments (JAR 2022) [S]; TikTok Creative Codes recommend 'clean and satisfying' edits [M].
satisfying-macro.needs: an extreme close-up texture with the real product sound; little or no music
satisfying-macro.ai_render_risk: medium: fluid and foam physics; the sound must be real or foley, not generated speech

count.source: TikTok 3-5 creatives per ad group; Symphony 3 variants per run; Meta creative diversity rating

shared_across_variants: primary keyword spoken and on screen by 3.0 s (DISC-01/02)
diversity.presenter_filter: presenter=ai drops ai_safe=false archetypes and every human_only template (D137)

testing_protocol.paid: one ad per variant in one ad set/ad group, same budget, same audience, launched together; read daily, decide at day 3 or 7
testing_protocol.instagram_trial_reels: post all variants as MANUAL trials the same day within a 2 h window; looks at 24, 48, 72 h; graduate the winner, never repost a loser as-is
testing_protocol.organic_other: alternate the variants across comparable slots (same weekday and hour band); treat as directional only
testing_protocol.looks: pre-registered only; no decisions between looks

primary.tiktok_paid: 2-second video views / impressions (TikTok reports 2 s and 6 s views; exact metric names UNVERIFIED)
primary.tiktok_organic: retention at 3.0 s from the retention curve (manual)

metrics.guardrail_rule: winner may not be worse than the primary by more than 10% relative on any guardrail

stats.model: Beta-Binomial per variant: holds ~ Binomial(n, p), p ~ Beta(a0 + holds, b0 + n - holds)
stats.prior: a0 = 20 * m, b0 = 20 * (1 - m), m = account's rolling median hold rate for the platform (fallback: platform median above)
stats.decision: pick variant v when P(v is best) >= 0.95 AND expected loss of choosing v <= 0.01, evaluated by 20,000 Monte Carlo draws

power_guide.note: normal approximation, 80% power, one-sided 95%; derived here

stats.futility: at the last look, if no variant has P(best) >= 0.80, keep the primary and log 'no difference'
stats.early_kill: drop a variant at any look when P(p < kill threshold) >= 0.90
stats.prior_update: update archetype and visual priors only from paid tests or >= 2 replicated organic wins

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.description: spoken hook length and time budget
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: n = len(lexicon.words(hook)); x = 1 if 4<=n<=8 and 0.3 + n/3.0 <= 3.0 else 0.6 if n == 3 else 0
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: D73; Kim 2024 ~8 words per sentence [M]; SFV speech-rate rule [S]

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.description: product, category, flaw or a number within the first 3 words
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: first 3 norm tokens intersect tokens of ctx product/category/category_pl/flaw/after or match \d; x = 1, words 4-5 -> 0.5, else 0
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: Meta: under-25 view time < 2 s [M]; 0.25 s recall [M]; OpusClip lead-with-the-thing [M]

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.description: product or category spoken by 3.0 s (search and relevance)
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: DISC-01 check on the hook cue; x in {0,1}
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: discovery-seo DISC-01 [P/M]; Creative Codes product early [S]

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.description: a concrete noun from ctx slots and/or a number
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: x = 0.5 per signal (number regex \b\d+\b|one..ten; any ctx noun phrase present), max 1
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: Loewenstein 1994 closable gap [S]; OpusClip specific-number pattern [A]

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.description: one or two concrete negative words
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: count NEG = {stop, don't, skip, quit, mistake, wrong, weak, ruins, fail, flaw, tired, wasted, lost}; x = 1 for 1, 0.8 for 2, 0.4 for >=3, 0 for none
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: Robertson 2023 +2.3% CTR per negative word [S]; Gligoric 2023 beta 0.18 [S]

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: x = 1 if presenter == 'human' and re '\b(I|my|me)\b'; 0 for ai (D137 gate handles misuse)
x = 1 if re '\byou(r)?\b' and (hook ends with '?' or starts with 'if you')
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: Lai & Farbrot 2014 self-referencing questions [M]; 'you' alone n.s. (Gligoric) [S]

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.description: signed: specific answerable question vs rhetorical or vague
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: if '?' in hook: x = +1 when it contains keyword or number and not re 'have you ever|did you know|guess what'; else -1; no '?' -> 0
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: CME 2016, Kuiken 2017, Jung 2022 negative; Lai & Farbrot 2014 positive [M]

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.description: signed: open loop whose promise the payoff pays
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: loop = '?' or re 'here's (why|what|the)|what changed|which wins|verdict|check this|before you'; x = +1 if loop and payoff_contract names the same measurable (D5/D35), -1 if loop and no match, 0.3 if no loop
x = 1 - max trigram Jaccard vs last 50 shipped hooks in niche (keyword tokens removed); x = 0 if first3 tokens equal any of last 10
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: Meta same-opening = same ad [M]; Motion hook fatigue warning [M]; TikTok FYF unoriginal rule [P]; baseline distinct ratio 28%

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: x = 1 if mean syllables/word <= 1.6 excluding ctx product tokens, and no clause nesting (<= 1 comma)
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: readability n.s. for headlines (Gligoric) [S]; BBC subtitle-rate research [S]: low weight

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.description: frame-0 overlay is a contiguous hook phrase or label carrying the keyword head noun
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: lexicon.overlay_is_clean(ov, hook); x = 1 if clean and contains keyword head noun, 0.8 label form, 0.6 clean without keyword, 0 otherwise
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: Mayer & Johnson 2008 brief key phrases aid retention [S]; D144; DISC-02

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.description: frame-0 visual prior and fit to the archetype
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: x = VISUAL_HOOKS[vt].prior * (1 if archetype in VISUAL_HOOKS[vt].best_archetypes else 0.6)
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: Motion 2026 formats [M]; OpusClip showcase [M]; Creative Codes [S]

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.description: research prior for the archetype, zeroed if its requirements are unmet
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: x = ARCHETYPES[a].prior if requires satisfied and (presenter == 'human' or ai_safe != false) else 0
x = 1 if re '^(hey|hi|hello|okay|ok|alright|welcome)\b|^so,|in today.?s video|let me tell you|have you ever wondered'
x = 1 if lexicon.SLOP or lexicon.VAGUE_HOOK or re '\b(amazing|insane|crazy|unreal|mind-?blowing|obsessed|game.?changer|life.?changing)\b'
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: Robertson 2023: positive words lower CTR [S]; Meta sensational phrasing [P]

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: x = 1 on any RISKY_PHRASES entry with class 'clickbait'; also '!!' or an all-caps sentence of 4+ words
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.evidence: Meta clickbait guidelines [P]; YouTube clickbait policy [P]; D35

HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.description: urgency or scarcity without a supplied offer and deadline
HOOK_SCORE_FEATURES.detector: x = 1 on RISKY_PHRASES class 'urgency' when prompt has no offer/deadline (D158)

RISKY_PHRASES.why: sensational withholding phrase named by Meta
withholds the payoff to farm watch time

RISKY_PHRASES.regex: \bsecret (to|behind)\b|\bthey don'?t want you to know\b|\bindustry (doesn'?t|does not) want\b
RISKY_PHRASES.why: promises a secret demo/review payoffs cannot reveal
sensationalism without information
unverifiable claim about others; baseline fallback frame
excessive punctuation or an all-caps sentence (4+ words); case-sensitive
attention bait that promises nothing
comment and vote baiting
share baiting; sends must be earned
tag baiting
react baiting

PROPOSED_RULES.rule: script carries 3-4 hook_variants besides the primary; every pair differs in visual_type, archetype, first 3 tokens and on_screen; trigram Jaccard <= 0.2 with keyword tokens removed; <= 2 openings per cluster
PROPOSED_RULES.source: Meta same-opening guidance [M]; TikTok 3-5 creatives [S]; VARIANT_POLICY

PROPOSED_RULES.rule: every opening's archetype is in VARIANT_POLICY.payoff_compat[payoff_type] and all openings share one payoff_contract
presenter=ai: no opening uses an archetype with ai_safe=false or a human_only template; lexicon.AI_FIRST_PERSON clean
archetype requirements met: price-anchor needs a prompt price (D37), proof-first a prompt proof (D136), 'new' templates a newness fact, offer an offer and deadline (D158)
no RISKY_PHRASES hit in any opening's dialogue, on_screen or frame-0 direction unless allow_if holds
payload (product/category/flaw/number) within the first 3 spoken words; first word starts <= 0.3 s; keyword spoken by 3.0 s (DISC-01)
PROPOSED_RULES.source: Meta view-time statement [M]; SFV rule 2; DISC-01

PROPOSED_RULES.rule: each opening's overlay passes overlay_is_clean, holds the keyword head noun or a label pair, and stays on screen from 0.0 s to the end of the spoken hook (>= 3.0 s)
primary = argmax hook_score among openings passing gates; primary >= 60, each alternate >= 50; store score and top-3 feature contributions in script.json
per 30-seed cell and per run: fallback hooks 0%; hook distinct ratio >= 0.60; distinct-2 >= 0.20; no first-3-token repeat within the last 10 hooks of a niche
the noun named in words 1-3 is visible in the frame-0 direction, and visual_type is in the archetype's best list or has prior >= 0.6

maker.note: How vsp.hooks maps the research onto viral_script_maker: payoff type per (concept, format) — the payoff beat each branch of build_beats writes; 'fix' is the advice branch (FIRST 3 SECONDS: trigger, hook, contract), which VARIANT_POLICY does not cover (our inference, A). Visual and audio sentences paraphrase VISUAL_HOOKS.needs and §2.4; the voice enters on the maker's VERBAL HOOK cue (0.5 s).

ai_visual_notes.real_footage: Real footage required: a generated result is not proof, so never render this frame.
ai_visual_notes.render: AI render: neutral hands, no invented logos.

audio_cues.product-in-action: The product's own sound from frame 0; the voice comes in on the hook cue over it.
audio_cues.result-reveal: One soft reveal hit at frame 0, then the voice on the hook cue; no music drop.
audio_cues.before-after-split: A single swoosh on the split, then the voice on the hook cue.
audio_cues.problem-state: The problem's own sound first, then the voice on the hook cue.
audio_cues.pov-hands: Close-miked hands-on sound from frame 0; the voice on the hook cue.
audio_cues.face-reaction: No music under the first line; the voice on the hook cue.
audio_cues.text-first: The voice on the hook cue over a low music bed from the platform library.
audio_cues.unboxing: Real packaging sound at frame 0, then the voice on the hook cue.
audio_cues.comparison: Both sides' real sound on the same beat, then the voice on the hook cue over a low bed.
audio_cues.day-counter: That day's ambient sound; the voice on the hook cue names the day.
audio_cues.satisfying-macro: Real product sound only, little or no music; the voice on the hook cue.

maker.audio_product_cue: The product's real sound is the hook: volume-up card at frame 0, the voice on the hook cue.

product.product-in-action: Frame 0: {subject} mid-task, hands in frame, visible motion by 0.5 s, its real sound up.
product.result-reveal: Frame 0: the finished result first, {subject} beside it, a real capture the payoff re-shows in context.
product.before-after-split: Frame 0: split screen, before left and after right, matched framing and light, {subject} in both halves.
product.problem-state: Frame 0: the problem at its worst, honestly shown, with {subject} entering the frame by 3 s.
product.pov-hands: Frame 0: first-person angle, the viewer's hands already using {subject}, motion by 0.5 s.
product.face-reaction: Frame 0: the presenter's face with {subject} in the same frame, the reaction already under way.
product.text-first: Frame 0: a 3-word card over moving footage of {subject}; the card is added in the edit, never drawn in-frame.
product.unboxing: Frame 0: the package already opening mid-action, {subject} half out; real packaging only, no invented branding.
product.comparison: Frame 0: {subject} side by side with the usual alternative on the same test, same framing, no brand names.
product.day-counter: Frame 0: a DAY {n} label over real footage from that day, {subject} in progress.
product.satisfying-macro: Frame 0: extreme close-up of {subject} in motion (texture, surface, detail), its own sound up, little or no music.

streak.day-counter: Frame 0: a DAY {n} label over real footage from that day, {subject} in progress.
streak.problem-state: Frame 0: the old habit at its worst, honestly shown ({habit}), before day 1.
streak.text-first: Frame 0: a 3-word card over moving footage of {subject}; the card is added in the edit, never drawn in-frame.
streak.before-after-split: Frame 0: split screen, day 1 left and day {n} right, same place, same framing and light.
streak.face-reaction: Frame 0: the creator's face on day {n}, the day counter in the same frame.
streak.result-reveal: Frame 0: the day-{n} result first (the log, {subject} finished), a real capture.
streak.pov-hands: Frame 0: first-person angle, hands mid-routine on day {n}, motion by 0.5 s.

advice.text-first: Frame 0: a 3-word card over the creator mid-gesture on {subject}; the card is added in the edit, never drawn in-frame.
advice.face-reaction: Frame 0: the creator's face to camera mid-sentence on {subject}, no intro.
advice.problem-state: Frame 0: the failing example first ({subject} gone wrong), honestly shown.
advice.comparison: Frame 0: two examples side by side, the weak one and the fixed one ({subject}), same framing.
advice.result-reveal: Frame 0: the fixed example first ({subject} done right), a real capture.
advice.pov-hands: Frame 0: first-person angle, hands already working on {subject}, motion by 0.5 s.
